claims.text: The anomalous stress–strain and thermoelastic behavior of HfNbTaTiZr is primarily governed by coupling between cold-work-induced dislocation networks and precipitate-induced thermal-expansion mismatch.
The initial as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a single BCC phase.
Controlled cold rolling generates a high density of dislocations in HfNbTaTiZr.
Aging HfNbTaTiZr at 600–800 °C initiates fine nanoscale precipitate formation.
A post-aging stress-relief or homogenization anneal largely removes cold-work stored energy and residual internal stresses.
Cold-work-induced dislocations remain as stored energy and introduce lattice distortions.
Plastic deformation is controlled by dislocation slip and depends on dislocation density.
The aging-induced precipitates have a lower lattice constant than the parent BCC phase.
The aging-induced precipitates have a thermal-expansion coefficient different from that of the HfNbTaTiZr matrix.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between precipitates and the BCC matrix generates internal thermal stresses.
Dislocation-associated and precipitate-mismatch stresses jointly increase elastic modulus at ambient and intermediate temperatures.
Dislocation-associated and precipitate-mismatch stresses jointly increase microhardness.
The internal stresses alter high-temperature dislocation pinning and climb kinetics at 1250 °C.
Relative to a stress-relieved baseline, the cold-rolled and aged alloy will have higher yield strength.
Relative to a stress-relieved baseline, the cold-rolled and aged alloy will have higher microhardness.
Relative to a stress-relieved baseline, the cold-rolled and aged alloy will have a higher elastic modulus from room to intermediate temperatures.
Relative to a stress-relieved baseline, the cold-rolled and aged alloy will likely have a lower creep rate at 1250 °C because of stronger dislocation pinning.
Elastic modulus should be measured over 293–1100 K, aging should be performed at 600–800 °C, and tensile creep should be tested at approximately 1250 °C.
The controlled comparison is between cold-rolled and aged samples with and without an additional stress-relief anneal.
Failure of stress relief to reduce modulus, microhardness, and yield strength or alter creep rate would falsify residual internal stress as the unified governing cause.
